page: The Microsoft Azure F16ads_v7 is a virtual machine instance from the Fadsv7 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, operating with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 1890 GB local disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not feature complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations all placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-core performance is strong, with Geekbench multi-core and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranking in the top 25%, though stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores fall into the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes show average performance, while Passmark memory scores rank in the top 25%. For specialized workloads, image and text processing benchmarks achieve top-tier results, and small-model LLM text generation performs in the top 10%. Medium and large model LLM inference operations remain in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F16ads_v7 offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated high-frequency AMD EPYC cores with a substantial 1890 GB local storage allocation. This setup avoids the premium cost of GPU-accelerated hardware while delivering top-tier single-threaded execution speeds. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for general-purpose workloads, database operations, and text or image processing pipelines. It is also appropriate for software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference tasks where dedicated CPU execution is required without the need for massive memory arrays.
